notes: Check batch 2026-10-30-check-2 for order-report: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and model_id matching their tier; each result.json records head e66d728 with uncommitted true and skill_hash fa83a48f..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the new captures paragraph ("A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn") and the current with sentence ("One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail"). skills_listed is 83 for all four. All four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there (no Decimal package is available, which is why compiles carries Decimal warnings); the Sonnet runs' doctests pass (1 each, compiled to .beam). A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), a zero-completed customer left out of top_customers in all four, empty results for [] and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-2 and sonnet-2 raise FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount (Decimal.parse/1 takes only binaries; the prompt says amounts are strings); haiku-2 reports the last order as a DateTime (:last_order_at) where the prompt asks for a date; no rule in the list covers these, so they are noted in the summaries only.

The captures rule is graded against the new text. Its new paragraph decides every fn: "A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn: the body goes on the line after the `->`, and `end` closes it on a line of its own" and "A one-line `fn {name, kind} -> {name, root_view(doc, name, kind)} end` is a capture that could not be written, squeezed onto the head's line". No run writes a fn that binds nothing, so "A `fn -> now end` that binds nothing may stay on one line" decides nothing. Every fn, by run: haiku-1 three, all binding names and all multi-line (body on the next line, end on its own line): lines 120-122 Enum.map(fn {customer_id, customer_orders} ->, lines 138-140 Map.new(fn {currency, amounts} ->, lines 152-154 Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} ->; clean under the first sentence. Haiku-2 writes no fn. Sonnet-1 four, all binding names: lines 90-98 Enum.reduce_while(..., fn {row, index}, {:ok, orders} -> (wraps a case), lines 155-157 Map.new(fn {customer_id, customer_orders} ->, lines 173-175 Map.new(fn {currency, amounts} -> are multi-line, clean under the first sentence; line 182 |> Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end) is one line, violated under the second sentence. Sonnet-2 four, all binding names and all multi-line: lines 83-91 Enum.reduce_while(..., fn {row, index}, {:ok, parsed} -> (wraps a case), lines 142-144 Map.new(fn {customer_id, customer_orders} ->, lines 162-169 Map.new(fn {currency, currency_orders} -> (a three-step body), lines 176-178 Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} ->; clean. The same sort_by key fn is multi-line in haiku-1 and sonnet-2 and one line in sonnet-1. The rule's first paragraph, unchanged since 2026-10-30-check, also decides haiku-2: line 57 &{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id} uses &1 twice, violated under "When the body does more than one call, would need `&3`, or passes `&2` before `&1` or the same placeholder twice, write `fn` with named arguments" (the earlier check batch found no capture of this shape). Result: haiku 1 of 2 violated (haiku-2, placeholder twice), sonnet 1 of 2 violated (sonnet-1, one-line fn).

The `->` clause rule is graded against its current text, whose last sentence now reads "A `fn` passed as an argument follows the capture rule instead: when it binds names, its body goes on the line after the `->` whatever its length" (it replaces "A one-line `fn` passed as an argument is outside this rule"). Sonnet-1's one-line fn at line 182 is therefore graded under the captures rule only, not here. Case clauses measured after indentation: longest one-line clause haiku-1 66 (line 84, with a guard), haiku-2 60 (line 134), sonnet-1 60 (line 141), sonnet-2 60 (line 129); none over 70. Sonnet-1 (lines 91-97) and sonnet-2 (lines 84-90) write their reduce_while case broken with a blank line between clauses although the longer clause, {:error, reason} -> {:halt, {:error, {:invalid_order, index, reason}}}, is exactly 70 characters and fits; held clean as in 2026-10-30-check, since the rule forbids a long clause on one line, not breaking one at the limit. 0 of 4 violated.

The with rule is graded against its current text. It now has the sentence "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`", which the 2026-10-30-check grade does not cite (its skill_hash, a98d7073..., differs from this batch's); that batch held sonnet-2's identical |> case do pass-through as not a violation. Here it decides sonnet-1: lines 99-102 |> case do / {:ok, orders} -> {:ok, Enum.reverse(orders)} / {:error, _reason} = error -> error is violated (fix: with {:ok, orders} <- Enum.reduce_while(...) do {:ok, Enum.reverse(orders)} end, after naming the reduce result). Haiku-1 is decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`" and "A body that calls another function that can fail makes that call the second step": parse_rows/2 at lines 55-59 is a one-step with whose body, line 57 parse_rows(rest, [order | orders]), is the tail-recursive call that returns {:error, ...} for any later bad row, so it is violated by the text as written. The shape is new and the text's two fixes (a case, or the recursive call as a second <- step whose body returns {:ok, orders}) both read worse than the with; I would keep the verdict, because the text names no exception for a tail call, and suggest the rule author decide whether a body that only returns the same result shape counts as one that can fail. Clean shapes: all four write build/1 as a one-step with whose body builds the report and cannot fail, no else (haiku-1 line 46, haiku-2 line 43, sonnet-1 line 78, sonnet-2 line 75); the multi-step withs have eight steps (haiku-1) or three (haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), none with an else or a nested case; the per-field normalizers are cases that map the error; the reduce_while cases (haiku-2 lines 93-96, sonnet-1 lines 91-97, sonnet-2 lines 84-90) wrap results in {:cont, ...} or {:halt, ...}, which is not a pass-through. Result: haiku 1 of 2 violated (haiku-1), sonnet 1 of 2 violated (sonnet-1).

Other rules in the list, same standard as 2026-10-23/grades/order-report-skill.json and 2026-10-30-check. The do: rule: every do: body is a tuple or a single call (haiku-1 lines 51, 53; parse_status/1 clauses everywhere; the catch-all clauses of haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2), no do: body holds a fn or a capture with a call, no run writes if or for, and each block clause beside a do: clause is set apart by a blank line. Pipelines: no pipeline on one line, none pipes a single step, none starts with a kind or mode argument; sonnet-1 pipes into case at line 99, which no rule forbids. Enum/Map: all four group with Enum.group_by then Map.new or Enum.map; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count with frequencies_by, haiku-2 counts the filtered list that also feeds the totals (Enum.count), held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: haiku-2 and sonnet-2 prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order; haiku-1 and sonnet-1 reverse. Naming, dates, money, atoms and processes: all four clean. The multi-line heads of haiku-2's, sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's parse_order/1 bind the five required keys with a catch-all clause below, so the keys select by presence and the head rule is held clean. Outside the list: the @doc of build/1 has no ## Examples in haiku-1 and haiku-2 (Comments rule), as earlier batches listed; sonnet-1's {:ok, %{...}} and {:ok, %Order{...}} at lines 79-83 and 115-122 are returned tuples, not call arguments, so the named-argument rule lists nothing. No other violation was found.
